what_happened.line: The commission ordered the 228 West Street owner to restore drainage trenches to their original condition by spring, with notice to the agent first.
It approved a notice of intent for retaining walls at 72 Hemlock Drive, with the face of the wall staked and approved by the agent, after debate over grandfathering.
It approved the common driveway crossing at 41 and 47 Reservoir Road and the 69 Colburn Street septic replacement.
It approved the conservation restriction for the 994 Northfield Road solar site as drafted and backed sending it to the state.
Votes to pay for a 21E study from the land acquisition trust fund and to continue three hearings to January 15 were not audible in the minutes.

why_it_matters: The conservation restriction on the solar site and the choice to pay for the 21E study from the land acquisition trust fund, not the forestry account, bear on how town conservation money is used.
The Hemlock Drive and West Street decisions show how the commission treats old walls and altered drainage near wetlands, which affects what nearby property owners may build or must undo.
watch_next: Continued hearings for 54 Plantation Drive, the DPW culvert and the Nancy Bell retaining wall return on January 15.
A site inspection at 139 Northfield Road was planned for Saturday, January 11, and could slip to spring if snow covers the ground.

what_happened.line: The Commission approved the order of conditions for the Lake Shirley weed-management program for five years, with its special conditions as amended.
Two conditions were changed: the annual report and late-summer survey must come from a contractor other than the treatment contractor, and the 48-hour default algae-treatment line was struck.
The Commission issued negative determinations for 238 Prospect Street and 152 Flynn Road, and approved a notice of intent for a dwelling and septic system.
It adopted updated wetland regulations and signed a settlement agreement for 101 Pleasant Street that forgives fines in exchange for a smaller payment.
Hearings on the culvert, 51 Fire Road, Sunset Lane and 260 Pallulah Road were continued to November 6, and Island Road to November 20.

why_it_matters: The Lake Shirley order sets who tests and reports on the lake's weed treatment for the next five years, which affects lake users and the cost carried by the volunteer group running the program.
The updated wetland regulations apply to future building or yard work near wetlands, rivers and lakes in town, and the trust-fund spending on a land appraisal draws on conservation money.
watch_next: November 6: continued hearings for the culvert, 51 Fire Road, Sunset Lane and 260 Pallulah Road, with a site visit to Pallulah Road the Saturday at 9 a.m. before.
November 20: Island Road hearing, after the applicant revises plans to keep structures outside the 30-foot zone.
